screens.title: Adverts want your coins

cards.caption: An advert is made to make you want something.
You decide. An advert does not.

screens.penny: Adverts are not naughty, {name}. They just want your coins.

screens.prompt: What is an advert trying to do?
screens.rightMessage: Yes, {name}! An advert is made to make something look exciting.
screens.wrongMessage: Good try, {name}! An advert's job is to make you want to buy the thing.

screens.prompt: An advert says a toy is the best thing ever. Is that always true?
screens.rightMessage: That's right, {name}! The advert wants to sell it, so we check for ourselves.
screens.wrongMessage: Good try, {name}! Adverts show the best bits. It's smart to check for yourself.
screens.retryIntro: Let's think about that advert again, {name}.

screens.story: An advert says a toy will make Raj the happiest kid alive. It costs all his coins.

options.label: Stop, think, and ask a grown-up
options.outcome: Raj asks his dad. Together they see it is a small plastic toy. Raj keeps his coins.

options.label: Believe the advert and buy it
options.outcome: Raj spends every coin. The toy is much smaller than it looked on the screen.

screens.rightMessage: Yes, {name}! Stop, think, and ask a grown-up.
screens.wrongMessage: Good try, {name}! Adverts show the very best bits. Asking a grown-up helps.

screens.title: You did it, {name}!
screens.message: You choose. An advert doesn't choose for you.
